approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and fills each batch with the first neighbors admitted by its inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes current even when its score is worse, while an independent archive retains the best observations. Memory blocks only qualifying two-sign reversals from one selected transition; partial reversals can remain admissible. When accepted neighbors tie for the maximum score, canonical spelling currently decides which becomes the next source.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, prefer the one that undoes the fewest motif-occurrence changes from the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical order if that comparison also ties. This gives the most recent structural direction a chance to persist at the same accepted score. Earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms or greater distance from the current molecule. This rule instead compares the directions and magnitudes of two consecutive moves; it can prefer less structural displacement and does not reward compactness. The existing proposal generator and memory restrictions remain the Parent's.

hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with the smallest capped inverse motif-occurrence overlap with the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.

finding_summary.headline: Five tied choices reduced immediate motif overlap, but the predicted score gain did not appear
finding_summary.insights: This rules out failure to execute the tie rule as the explanation for the absent score gain. Reducing immediate motif-count reversal can change the search without shortening its plateaus or improving its aggregate endpoint. The five choices overlap within only two task/seed continuations, so the later deco_hop improvement cannot be credited independently to each of its four changed ties. The count statistic also has a narrower chemical meaning than preserving the last physical edit: it can penalize extending an ethyl group to propyl, or match a motif lost on one ring to a motif introduced on another. One changed choice preserves a C#S-O group by extending an unrelated N-alkyl chain, while another replaces a carbonyl carbon with sulfur. The molecular assessment finds that the altered paths retain or add questionable sulfur, oxygen-oxygen and sulfur-halogen connections, with no change to the pooled highest-scoring molecule on any task. Lower overlap therefore supplies no evidence of improved feasibility or more useful chemistry. Whether a comparison tied to actual edited sites or chemically useful arrangements would improve these choices remains open.
finding_summary.results: The rule changed five of 26 tied maximum decisions across two of fifteen task/seed sessions. Each change kept the same accepted score and reduced overlap with the previous move to zero; the corresponding lexical choices would have reversed eight motif occurrences in total. All five choices had later evaluations. Across the complete walks, inverse overlap during score plateaus fell from 26 to 14 occurrences, yet plateau transitions increased from 49 to 52. The three-seed macro mean was 0.52169764, compared with 0.52175912 for the parent: a paired change of -0.00006147, below the predeclared +0.002 improvement. The changed deco_hop continuation finished at 0.61072664 versus 0.60921826, while median_2 finished at 0.18849201 versus 0.19092251. The other thirteen full molecule/score trajectories were identical. The local mechanism is confirmed; the predicted score benefit is refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and carbonyl families repeatedly acquire unusual sulfur, reactive attachments and dense cages with unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-1aba3c4825a4 produces medium-sized to large, heavily substituted ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran carboxamides, aryl ketones, fused nitrogen heterocycles, cyclic amines and lactams coexist with much less conventional sulfur-rich cages. Each supplied task digest covers 900 evaluated rows, including 870 optimizer proposals over seeds 0, 1 and 2. Ring-closure-token presence is 1.0 in every proposal set. Aromatic-token presence in the fixed task order is 0.9563, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7184; these are molecule-presence rates, not fractions of aromatic atoms. Every task has charged-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. The neutral spelling does not imply absence of potentially basic amines. Passive RDKit reading of the full supplied trajectories confirms ring and aromatic content and graph parseability, but does not establish conformational feasibility, chemical stability or synthesis. Structural diversity is moderate: different seeds reach different ring families, while the displayed score leaders often cluster around one heavily modified framework. Direct Child/Parent comparison finds identical molecule/score records in thirteen of fifteen task/seed trajectories. The differences are confined to deco_hop seed 2 and median_2 seed 1; the highest-scoring molecule pooled over seeds remains identical to the Parent on every task. The changed trajectories introduce different chemistry without resolving the recurring liabilities. All five objectives have trajectories. Size, bond-prevalence and Parent comparisons below are passive counts from those files, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-09-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Score readings describe observed molecular associations and do not infer an unseen target structure, activity mechanism or score for an unobserved analogue.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes current even when its score is worse, while an independent archive retains the best observations. Memory blocks only qualifying two-sign reversals from one selected transition; partial reversals can remain admissible. approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, prefer the one that undoes the fewest motif-occurrence changes from the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical order if that comparison also ties. This gives the most recent structural direction a chance to persist at the same accepted score. Earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms or greater distance from the current molecule. This rule instead compares the directions and magnitudes of two consecutive moves; it can prefer less structural displacement and does not reward compactness. The existing proposal generator and memory restrictions remain the Parent's.
